summary: A Statalist forum thread from 2018 and 2021 in which users discuss importing and summarizing very large CSV files in Stata. Beckie Garvin asks how to analyze a 58-million-observation CSV, and Clyde Schechter suggests chunking it with runby but argues that analyzing the whole file is simpler. Leonardo Guizzetti reports that Stata can handle such files, citing a dummy-data test that imported 58M observations in a few minutes. In 2021 Shadi Shad reports that importing 1.5 GB CSV files takes hours and crashes Stata.
one_line: Statalist thread on handling and importing very large CSV files (up to 58 million observations) in Stata.
key_facts: Beckie Garvin's 2018 post describes a very large .csv file with 58 million observations and 24 variables.
Clyde Schechter's largest dataset at the time had 14,342,307 observations and 10 numeric variables.
Clyde Schechter reported that Stata took 37 seconds to calculate descriptive statistics on all 10 variables of that dataset.
Clyde Schechter's code uses the runby command, written by Robert Picard and Clyde Schechter and available from SSC, to split a CSV into chunks.
Clyde Schechter's example creates 6 chunks of about 10,000,000 observations each, saved as chunk1.dta through chunk6.dta.
Clyde Schechter argued that re-combining descriptive statistics from chunks could cost more time and risk errors than analyzing the whole dataset.
Leonardo Guizzetti noted that Stata/IC can have about 2 billion observations.
Leonardo Guizzetti wrote a 58-million-observation, 2-variable test file of about 1.0 GB that took about 10 minutes to export.
Leonardo Guizzetti reported that importing the 58-million-observation test file took a few minutes on his machine.
Leonardo Guizzetti reported that summ x, detail took about a minute on the 58-million-observation dataset.
In September 2021, Shadi Shad reported that a 1.53 GB CSV file took 2 hours to import and Stata stopped responding before the import completed.
Shadi Shad's 2021 post describes CSV files of 500 MB to 2 GB, with over 50 files in total in the directory E:/Comtradet1.
Shadi Shad's smallest file, 280 MB, imported successfully, while a 1.50 GB file kept Stata running for hours before it crashed.
